summary: Devils Island Light at the south-east end of the island at the entrance to Halifax Harbour: lit 1852, second tower 1877, the present red skeletal light; boat access only.

lens.note: fourth-order dioptric lens in the 1912-13 Marine report; NSLPS dates the fourth order to 1922

structures.note: west tower; discontinued 1949, 1950 or 1958 (sources differ); removed
east tower; Rowlett 'Inactive', 14 m (46 ft); lantern removed 1978; NSLPS says standing and operating; LF says decommissioned and left to the elements
present light at the south-east end; date 2009 (Rowlett) or 2011 (LF)
built in the 1930s (LF); flattened by a storm in 2012 (LF); in ruins per Rowlett

access.note: Reached only by boat. Grounds open, tower closed (LF; Rowlett).

events.note: brig Southampton, carrying flour, ran aground on the south-west point; all but one crew got ashore on lines
wooden octagonal lighthouse erected at a cost of 283 pounds; oil, after asphaltum gas plan failed

Keeper Benjamin Fulker and five men went out in a storm to rescue the Union's crew; Minister sent letters of thanks and $20 cheques
second, eastern wooden octagonal tower; two fixed white lights shown from 15 October 1877
new lantern and lighting apparatus on the western tower to equalize the two lights
Department of Marine life-saving station established on the island (separate station; NSLPS: lifeboat stationed 1885-1940)
life-saving station coxswain G. E. De Young resigned in May; Benjamin H. Hennebery appointed
fishing schooner Montana went ashore in a gale on 26 April (1909, inferred from the fiscal year ended 31 March 1910) at Devil's Island; got off again with the lifeboat's help (life-saving station)
fiscal 1912-13 Marine report: east light apparatus improved by a fourth-order dioptric lens (OCR matched by position). NSLPS gives 1922
eastern light changed to flashing; western (1852) light discontinued; NSLPS gives 1949 for discontinuing the original tower and group flashing red
western light discontinued. Rowlett gives 1950 (list) and 1958 (entry); sources differ
made unwatched in 1967; last keeper Charles C. McDonald left the island (LF); NSLPS: automated by 1967
lantern room removed from the 1877 tower; light shown from a short mast on top (Rowlett)
light removed from the east tower early in 2009 and moved to a 6.5 m square skeletal tower at the southern tip (Rowlett). LF dates the new steel tower near the western site to 2011
storm flattened the keeper's dwelling built in the 1930s (LF); Rowlett: ruins

resolved_conflicts.explanation: First light 1852 (west, wooden octagonal tower; LF, NSLPS). The 1877 date in the record is the second, eastern tower (LF; Rowlett). Both are right for different towers.

The present light is red, LFl 6 s with flash 2 s and eclipse 4 s (Coast Guard list; Rowlett: red light, 2 s on, 4 s off). NSLPS records a flashing white characteristic from 1992 on the eastern tower, and the record's OSM white characteristic reflects that earlier light. The change date is not given.

notes_for_editor: Rich-ish evidence, with sharp disagreements. Sources: LighthouseFriends (narrative, roster, cites Department reports and books it does not reproduce), NSLPS (keeper list, dates), Rowlett (two entries, 2009 move), Coast Guard list (present light), and four Marine reports (life-saving station 1885; coxswain change 1905; Montana 1910; fourth-order lens 1912-13). Disagreements left open in the story: (1) the west light's end: 1949 (LighthouseFriends, NSLPS), 1950 (Rowlett list), 1958 (Rowlett entry); (2) the present light's move: 2009 (Rowlett) against 2011 (LighthouseFriends); (3) the 1877 tower's status: NSLPS standing and operating, Rowlett inactive, LighthouseFriends decommissioned; (4) fourth-order lens: 1912-13 (Marine report, OCR matched by position, 'Devil island, east'; scan p. 49, printed p. 42) against 1922 (NSLPS). The Marine entry is the primary record; the NSLPS date may refer to a later change; not settled. Wikipedia gives a 1837 day beacon date and a 1949 demolition, but its 1837 claim cites a local history we did not read; not used. Keeper spellings: McDonald (LighthouseFriends) against MacDonald (NSLPS); Fulker start 1861 (LighthouseFriends) against 1863 (NSLPS). The 1905 coxswain Benjamin H. Hennebery is not linked to keeper Benjamin A. Henneberry (1949-53); the sources connect neither. The Dominion life-saving station (1885 onward) is a separate station on the same island; its coxswains are named in the story, not in the roster, and it may need its own record. Do not confuse with the Devils Island Light in Wisconsin (Lake Superior) or the Devils Island pages of Michigan (Terry Pepper). Chronicling America was not searched for this station. The 1852 facts come from LighthouseFriends and NSLPS only, because no pre-1900 Nova Scotia report is in the corpus. The 1911 Marine casualty list records 'Stranded near Devil's Island' with no vessel or date; not used. The 1906 inspector's remark that no wreck needed the lifeboats in the year is general to his stations; not used. Living people: keepers after about 1960 (McDonald, the Henneberrys, Messenger) appear only as LighthouseFriends and NSLPS print them, in public role. No general context used. The Montana date assumes the life-saving section of the 1910 report covers calendar 1910; the report does not say so on the page read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: all 67 evidence quotes were found on the first run. Story changes: the Southampton sentence reordered (wreck 1850, petition 1851); 'finished in 1859' changed to 'built'; the Montana date: the life-saving section of the report for the fiscal year ended 31 March 1910 gives only '26 April', and that fiscal year begins 1 April 1909, so the date is 26 April 1909 by inference (wreck date and event year changed to 1909; a human should confirm); the Coast Guard list removed as a source for ownership (it names no owner; Rowlett and LighthouseFriends do); fiscal years given (the lens entry is in the report for the fiscal year ended 31 March 1913); the present-light sentence footnoted to the Coast Guard list; 'De Young' spelled as the 1905 report prints it (DeYoung). Image check: the 1912-13 'Devil island, east' row (archive scan p.49, printed p.42) was viewed in the archive viewer; the station name and the 4th-order dioptric lens entry sit on the same row, consistent with the OCR. Same-name check: the 1910 aids list also has Devil Island on Lake Huron (day beacons); the Montana entry is in the life-saving section and the lifeboat places it at the Nova Scotia station.
